doc.title: Types
doc.paragraph: Adaptive Script uses a TypeScript-like type syntax with Adaptive data types as leaves (integer, string, boolean, object, array, any, void, and the other registered data types)—not JavaScript primitive names. Types annotate variables, function parameters and returns, and script-local type / interface declarations.

Script types are separate from adaptive object types and value meta. Object-type validation at the adapter and request layer is unchanged. Script interface and object type literals are structural shapes for checking only.
T[] and Array<T> are the same array type. Optional properties use ?. Unions use |; intersections use &. Function types use (params) => Return.
Types are always parsed and stored. Checking is off by default so existing scripts keep working. Opt in with environment flags or the #typecheck pragma.

list.item: compile:typeCheck — compile-time checks when the right-hand side type is known, and runtime checks on assignment and script function parameters.
compile:typeCheckCompileOnly — compile-time only (wins if both mode flags are set).
compile:noImplicitAny — require annotations when checking is active (missing type is otherwise treated as any).
compile:strictNullChecks — stricter handling of null / undefined.
compile:strict — enables typeCheck, noImplicitAny, and strictNullChecks.

doc.paragraph: Flags can be set from the host environment or with flag_set in scripts (for example in tests).
In statement position, #typecheck sets checking policy for the rest of that compile unit (and evaluation on the same execution context):

Mode tokens: off / false, on / full / true, compileOnly. Option tokens: noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, strict. A trailing semicolon is required. #typecheck off; clears the mode flags and the related policy options for that unit.

list.item: Leaf data types (for example integer vs string).
Array types: value must be an array; element types are checked when the value is an inspectable array.
Tuples: array length and per-position types when inspectable.
Object / interface shapes: required properties must be present; property values must match declared types; extends bases are checked. Extra properties on the value are allowed (structural typing).
Function types: value must be a function (parameter/return structural matching may grow later).

doc.paragraph: Unannotated bindings and external / adaptive I/O are treated as any at compile time unless noImplicitAny is set. Runtime adaptive dataType and object-type meta rules still apply independently of script type checking.
